description: PROP-005's FIND-003 extension (verification-architecture.md:69) asserts driver-level bit-identity ONLY for `requiredBaseUnits` across three call sites (checkSourceFunded, Skip amount_in, BaseSigner tx amount) -- it does not assert that the driver's actual runtime argument to checkSourceFunded's `minGasWei` parameter equals `MIN_GAS_WEI`. Symmetrically, PROP-013's FIND-002(iter4) boundary fixtures (verification-architecture.md:77) test `verifySettlement` in isolation with a TEST-SUPPLIED `toleranceBps=50`, never asserting the driver's actual runtime argument to `verifySettlement`'s `toleranceBps` parameter equals `TOLERANCE_BPS`. The Verification Strategy's own Tier-2 summary confirms this scoping explicitly: 'PROP-005 additionally pins the MIN_GAS_WEI... literal against a 0n-default defect and, per FIND-003, asserts driver-level bit-identity of requiredBaseUnits across all three call sites... mirroring PROP-019's discipline' (verification-architecture.md:110-113) -- the driver-level identity treatment is explicitly attributed to requiredBaseUnits only; minGasWei gets only the isolated-pure-function-fixture treatment. The Tier-1 summary makes the identical scoping admission for TOLERANCE_BPS: 'PROP-013 additionally pins the TOLERANCE_BPS = 50 literal against two boundary fixtures' (verification-architecture.md:96-100) -- again describing only isolated pure-function boundary fixtures, no driver-level wiring assertion. A driver implementation that internally hardcodes or derives a DIFFERENT (weaker) minGasWei (e.g. defaults to 0n, or reads an unvetted value) when calling checkSourceFunded, or a different (looser) toleranceBps when calling verifySettlement, would pass every currently-specified PROP in this document -- PROP-005's MIN_GAS_WEI-literal fixture and PROP-013's boundary fixtures both call the PURE functions directly with the correct literal supplied AS A TEST INPUT, which proves only that the pure comparison logic is correct given that value; neither proves the driver actually supplies that value at its own call site. This is precisely the class of defect FIND-003 (iteration-4) identified for requiredBaseUnits ('capUsd() and toBaseUnits() each passing their own isolated unit tests is explicitly NOT sufficient evidence that this requirement holds -- only the driver-level call-argument assertion is', behavioral-spec.md:313-315), left unaddressed for its two sibling constants pinned in this same iteration. Concrete failure modes this permits, both passing every currently-specified PROP: (1) a driver bug defaulting minGasWei to 0n when calling checkSourceFunded reaches exactly the 'partially-fundable swap that dies mid-signature' scenario REQ-003's own edge case (behavioral-spec.md:199-200, 212-214) names as the thing this precondition exists to prevent; (2) a driver bug using a looser toleranceBps than 50 when calling verifySettlement lets REQ-007 declare success on a materially worse-than-quoted fill, exactly the failure mode REQ-007's edge case (behavioral-spec.md:375-378) exists to prevent.

evidence.snippet: PROP-005... EXTENDED per FIND-003 with a driver-level cross-call-site identity assertion mirroring PROP-019's discipline: for a fixture's need/aktUsdPrice, the ACTUAL argument the driver passes into checkSourceFunded's requiredBaseUnits parameter, SkipApiClient.getRoute()'s amount_in argument, and BaseSigner.signAndBroadcast()'s tx-amount argument MUST all three be bit-identical bigints... [no equivalent clause for minGasWei anywhere in PROP-005, no equivalent clause for toleranceBps anywhere in PROP-013]

fix: Extend PROP-005 with a second driver-level assertion (mirroring the FIND-003 extension already present for requiredBaseUnits) that the driver's actual runtime argument to checkSourceFunded's minGasWei parameter is bit-identical to MIN_GAS_WEI, inspected via spy call arguments in the same test run -- and construct the fixture so a driver implementation using a hardcoded or stray minGasWei value distinct from MIN_GAS_WEI (e.g. 0n) would fail the assertion. Extend PROP-013 symmetrically with a driver-level assertion that verifySettlement's toleranceBps runtime argument is bit-identical to TOLERANCE_BPS, constructed so a driver using a looser toleranceBps would fail.
